official.deadline_central_display: 15 January (Regular Decision and Early Decision II); 1 November for Early Action and Early Decision I
official.deadline_note: There is no separate scholarship deadline: the Global Scholars Program Scholarship follows Clark's admission deadlines, which are 1 November for Early Decision I and Early Action and 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision. Spring-entry first-year applicants have a 1 November deadline. Transfer applicants apply on rolling windows (February 1 - June 1 for fall, September 1 - November 1 for spring).
official.application_cycle: Current admissions cycle: Early Decision I and Early Action 1 November (decisions late December / mid-January), Early Decision II and Regular Decision 15 January (decisions early March / late March)
official.status_note: Clark's application rounds are published with 1 November and 15 January deadlines for first-year applicants; international applicants follow the same deadlines as all other applicants, and all admitted students are automatically considered for merit scholarships.
benefits: Merit scholarship consideration for incoming international students, awarded by a scholarship committee on the strength of the admissions application

Membership of the Global Scholars Program for incoming international students who have demonstrated outstanding leadership in their home communities, with guidance from a designated Clark mentor and opportunities to build on their leadership skills
Automatic consideration for all international first-year merit scholarships, including the International Traina, International Achievement and International Jonas Clark Scholarships
Optional interview, which can also serve as a supplementary measure of English proficiency
eligibility: You are an international student if you are not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident (green card holders are not international)
Applying as a first-year undergraduate to Clark University by the Early Action / Early Decision (1 November) or Regular Decision / Early Decision II (15 January) deadline
A separate essay must be submitted to be considered for the Global Scholars Program Scholarship, unlike the first three international merit scholarships which are automatic
All international students must complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form, available on the applicant status portal once they have applied
Applicants must be able to document English proficiency if English is not their native language
requirements: Common Application or Coalition Application with Scoir; there is no application fee
Transcripts covering the last three years of education (for 6-3-3 systems such as China, a middle school transcript showing the final year is also required)
Two letters of recommendation, one from a school counselor and one from a teacher (two academic teachers if the school has no counselor)
Proof of English language proficiency if English is not the native language
SAT or ACT scores, optional for all students including international applicants
International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form
A separate essay for Global Scholars Program Scholarship consideration
documents: Common Application or Coalition App with Scoir submission
Transcripts covering three complete years of education, in English or with certified English translations
Official or scanned TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, Pearson PTE or PEXT score report
International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form (from the applicant status portal)
selection_criteria: Merit-based scholarships are awarded on academic performance and other factors included in the application
Every applicant is automatically considered for most merit scholarships; no separate application is required for those
The Global Scholars Program Scholarship requires the additional essay, so it is decided on evidence not present in the standard application
Clark's admissions process is need-aware: an application may be denied if indicated financial need exceeds what the University can offer through scholarships and aid
coverage: Merit scholarship support towards the cost of attendance; Clark states that it is not able to offer financial assistance covering the full cost of attendance
Mentoring, guidance and leadership opportunities through the Global Scholars Program
application_method: Submit the Common Application (or Coalition App with Scoir) by the deadline for the chosen round
Submit the separate essay required for Global Scholars Program Scholarship consideration
Complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form in the applicant status portal after applying
Optional but encouraged: interview (in person, virtual, InitialView or Vericant), which can additionally evidence English proficiency
official.application_route: Apply to Clark through the Common App by 1 November (Early Action / Early Decision I) or 15 January (Regular Decision / Early Decision II), submit the Global Scholars essay, and complete the certification of finances form in the applicant portal.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents; Clark describes its international cohort as coming from over 80 nations
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award is specifically for international first-year applicants
official.duration: Undergraduate degree (four years); the published pages state no separate duration for the scholarship itself
official.description: The Global Scholars Program Scholarship is Clark University's merit award for incoming international undergraduates who have shown leadership in their home communities, and the only international first-year merit scholarship besides the Presidential Scholarship that requires an extra essay rather than automatic consideration.
official.program_type: University merit scholarship for international undergraduates (separate-essay track)
official.english_requirement: If English is not your native language you must provide an official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson PTE score. Clark publishes general indicators rather than strict minima: TOEFL iBT 85 overall with no sub-score below 20 (or 4.5 overall with no sub-score below 4 on the new scale from January 2026), IELTS 6.5 with no sub-score below 6, Duolingo 120 with no sub-score below 100, PTE 61 with no sub-score below 55, PEXT 71 with no sub-score below 65. Proficiency is assessed holistically and applicants who may benefit from support are routed into the 1-4 semester English for Academic Success Program.

verification.notes: The five international first-year merit scholarships, the separate-essay requirement for the Global Scholars Program Scholarship, the definition of an international student and the certification of finances form were read from Clark's financial aid FAQ; the English proficiency indicators, application checklist, cost of attendance and need-aware statement from the undergraduate admissions international page; the current round deadlines from the Clark apply page. Clark's own pages carry conflicting guidance on the need-based application route: the financial aid FAQ states the CSS Profile is not required and only the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form is asked for, while the admissions pages still direct applicants to the CSS Profile and the apply page mentions a Clark University International Student Aid Application. Figures circulated by third-party blogs (for example a $15,000-$25,000 range) were deliberately not used.

applicant_utility.summary: Everything hinges on the extra essay: the other three international first-year merit scholarships are automatic, but the Global Scholars Program Scholarship is invisible to the committee unless that essay is in, so treat it as a second mini-application rather than an afterthought. Apply by 1 November rather than 15 January if you can, because Clark gives Early Decision applicants more scholarship funding and a higher admission rate. Be realistic about the gap: Clark publishes a total cost of attendance of about $85,000 and says international students typically pay around $40,000 a year after aid, and it will deny an application outright if the need you declare is larger than what it can fund.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants from outside the U.S. with a documented record of community leadership who can either self-fund a substantial share or qualify for significant need-based aid.
application_readiness_checklist: Draft the Global Scholars essay separately and early - evidence of leadership in your home community, not general ambition, is what the programme page describes
Book the optional interview; it doubles as supplementary proof of English proficiency
Open the applicant status portal as soon as you have applied and complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form
Confirm which need-based application Clark wants from you this cycle (CSS Profile or the international certification form), because Clark's own pages disagree
Check that your transcripts cover three complete years, adding a middle school transcript if your country uses a 6-3-3 system
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the application without the Global Scholars essay, which removes you from this award entirely
Declared need larger than Clark can meet: the process is need-aware and the University states it cannot admit international students who require full funding
Incomplete transcripts - Clark states it cannot review an application with only two years of credentials
Leaving the certification of finances form late, since it only appears in the portal after you apply
Assuming a U.S. mailbox or an interview replaces the required English test evidence
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Against a published total cost of attendance of about $85,000 per year, international students typically still pay around $40,000 a year after scholarships and aid; on-campus work is limited and cannot cover a significant share, and U.S. rules bar off-campus employment.
document_audit: Documents must be in English, with both originals and certified translations acceptable
TOEFL, IELTS and PTE scores are preferred directly from the testing agency; a scan from you or your counselor is accepted, but Duolingo scores must come from the Duolingo portal itself
The certification of finances form cannot be started before you have applied, so sequence it after submission rather than alongside it
Recommendenders must be a counselor and a teacher, or two academic teachers if your school has no counselor
alerts: Need-aware admission means your funding request can decide the admission outcome, not just the award size
Early Decision is binding and Early Action is not - only Early Decision guarantees a decision and award before Thanksgiving

Clark also runs a Presidential Scholarship covering tuition, room and board for 3-5 students a year with no separate application, so your file is competing on two essay-optional and essay-required tracks at once
United World College graduates have an extra Davis grant of up to $15,000 a year that stacks with Clark merit aid
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One Common App submission by the round deadline, plus the Global Scholars essay and the portal certification form; the scholarship committee then reviews the whole file and no separate award application exists.
